intro: Pairs people mix up, with one rule to pick between them.

pairs.title: Tooltip, popover or hover card?
pairs.rule: If it only names something, it is a tooltip. If people act inside it, it is a popover. If it previews a person or link on hover, it is a hover card.

use.tooltip: A short label for an icon button. Text only, never links or buttons.
use.popover: A small panel with controls (share, filter, quick edit). Opens on click.
use.hover-card: A preview of a profile or link. Opens after a short hover or on focus.

pairs.title: Modal, drawer or bottom sheet?
pairs.rule: Ask for a decision in a modal, show detail or filters in a drawer, and offer actions on phones in a bottom sheet.

use.modal-dialog: One question that blocks progress: confirm, rename, delete.
use.drawer: Detail or filters next to a list the user still wants to see.
use.bottom-sheet: A short list of actions on mobile, within thumb reach.

pairs.title: Toast, banner or callout?
pairs.rule: Confirm something that just happened with a toast, announce something about the whole product with a banner, and explain something on this page with a callout.

use.toast-stack: "Saved", "Invite sent". Disappears on its own; never the only record of an error.
use.banner: Maintenance, a new release, a billing problem. One at a time, dismissible.
use.callout: A tip or warning inside content. Stays put.

pairs.title: Checkbox or toggle switch?
pairs.rule: A switch takes effect immediately; a checkbox waits for Save.

use.checkbox: Choices in a form that is submitted, or picking several items in a list.
use.toggle-switch: Settings that apply the moment you flip them.

pairs.title: Tabs or segmented control?
pairs.rule: Tabs switch between different content; a segmented control changes how the same content is shown.

use.segmented-control: 1D / 1W / 1M on one chart, or List / Grid on one list.

pairs.title: Radio group, radio cards or combobox?
pairs.rule: Up to five options: show them all as radios. Options that need a description or a price: radio cards. Long lists: a combobox people can type into.

use.radio-group: 2–5 short options that all fit on screen.
use.radio-cards: Plans or regions where each option needs a line of detail.
use.combobox: Time zones, countries, people: too many to show.

pairs.title: Accordion or disclosure?
pairs.rule: One hidden section is a disclosure; a stack of them is an accordion.

use.accordion: FAQs and grouped settings. Usually one open at a time.

pairs.title: Skeleton or spinner?
pairs.rule: If you know the layout that is coming, show a skeleton of it. If you do not, or the wait is a single action, use a spinner.

use.skeleton: Lists, cards and dashboards while data loads.
use.loaders: A button that is saving, or a short wait with no known shape.

pairs.title: Pagination or carousel?
pairs.rule: Use pagination when people need to find a specific item again; use a carousel only for a short, optional row of extras.

use.pagination: Search results, tables, archives: stable positions people can return to.
use.carousel: Related posts or a few highlights. Never for content people must see.

pairs.title: Dropdown menu, context menu or command palette?
pairs.rule: A dropdown holds actions for one visible button, a context menu repeats actions for the thing under the pointer, and a command palette reaches every action by typing.

use.dropdown-menu: "Actions" on a page header or row.
use.context-menu: Right-click on a file or a row. Always also reachable another way.

pairs.title: Progress bar, progress ring or meter?
pairs.rule: Progress is a task moving towards done; a meter is a level that can go up or down.

use.progress-bar: Uploads and multi-step tasks with room for a label.
use.progress-ring: Compact progress in a card corner or avatar.
use.meter: Storage used, quota, a score. Not a task.

pairs.title: Sidebar, top navbar or bottom nav?
pairs.rule: Marketing sites use a top navbar, apps with many sections use a sidebar, and phone apps with 3–5 destinations use a bottom nav.

use.navbar-mega: A public site with a product menu and a few pages.
use.bottom-nav: A mobile app's main destinations, always one tap away.

pairs.title: Count-up, odometer or flip clock?
pairs.rule: Count up once to reveal a figure, roll digits when a live number changes, and flip for a countdown people watch.

use.count-up: A headline KPI the first time it scrolls into view.
use.odometer: A live total that ticks up while people watch.
use.flip-clock: A countdown to a launch or a deadline.

pairs.title: Data table or virtual list?
pairs.rule: Compare values across columns in a table; scroll through thousands of single-line items in a virtual list.

use.data-table: Accounts, invoices, anything sorted and compared by column.
use.virtual-list: Logs, messages, events: long and mostly read top to bottom.
